I want to give you an opportunity to receive Christ, to make the most important decision of your life, to make that profession of faith that Trey was talking about. You can make that and take that by saying these words. Just say these after me. Just say, God, I admit to you the obvious that I'm a sinner. And I believe my sins have separated me from you, but I also believe that you sent Jesus Christ to die on the cross for my sins to rise again. And right now, I turn from my sins and turn to you, Jesus. I ask you to come into my life. I give you the heart supplies. I give you the brush and the paints and you do with me what you will. because I want to experience the ultimate freedom, the personification of liberty. So, Father, we thank You for this time. We ask all these things in Jesus' name. Amen.

explicit_propositions.text: Jesus said, 'If you hold to my teaching, you're really my disciples.'
Jesus declared, 'Then you will know the truth and the truth will set you free.'
Believers often fail to recognize their ultimate freedom in Christ.
Ava didn't understand that she had ultimate freedom in the yard.
The speaker paid a significant amount of money for Ava's freedom and well-being.
Chasing worldly desires like money or sex leads to enslavement.
The yard is manicured and fenced.
God financed believers' faith through the sacrifice of Jesus.
Ava understood that bolting in her pink sweater put her life in danger.
When believers turn away from God, they place their lives in danger.

assumptions.text: True freedom is only possible within a relationship with Christ.
Spiritual liberation requires both acceptance of Christ and ongoing adherence to His teachings.
Scriptural texts, particularly from the Gospel of John, contain authoritative truths about freedom and salvation.
People who claim to follow Christ may still live under the bondage of sin without realizing it.
The biblical narrative of liberation (e.g., Emancipation Proclamation) serves as a valid metaphor for spiritual freedom.
Divine love and pursuit of individuals are active, personal, and persistent, like a shepherd seeking a lost sheep.
Human beings possess inherent moral agency and the capacity to freely accept or reject divine grace.
Metaphors drawn from daily human experiences (like pet care or art) effectively communicate complex theological concepts.
The act of making a public profession of faith is a meaningful and transformative step toward genuine spiritual freedom.
Audience members are spiritually receptive and capable of responding positively to a direct invitation to faith.
